The new store is Apple’s seventh in the country, as the premium gadget-maker grows its retail presence in India by targeting its largest cities. Customers will be able to experience and buy Apple products, apart from accessing services and support directly, the company highlighted. Hyderabad houses Apple’s Research and Development and Retail Customer Care teams. The design language for Apple Kukatpally takes inspiration from pearls, in a nod to Hyderabad’s identity and historical legacy as the ‘City of Pearls.’ The iPhone-maker’s other retail locations in India include Apple BKC and Apple Borivali in Mumbai, Apple Saket and Apple Noida in Delhi NCR, Apple Hebbal in Bengaluru, and Apple Koregaon Park in Pune.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “Ahead of opening day, customers are invited to download exclusive Apple Kukatpally wallpapers and stickers, explore a curated Apple Music playlist inspired by the sounds of Hyderabad, and learn more about the upcoming store at apple.com/in/retail/kukatpally,” announced Apple in a press release.

articles.title: Yemen's Houthi-held capital hit after group targets Riyadh
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The exchanges between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen have become near-daily in the country's revived civil war

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Houthi media reported a series of Saudi airstrikes against territory held by the Iran-backed group including the capital Sanaa on Thursday (November 26, 2026), hours after it struck Riyadh. The exchanges between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen have become near-daily in the country's revived civil war, which first began more than a decade ago. The coalition, which backs Yemen's internationally recognised government, said during the night that it had intercepted two ballistic missiles launched by the Houthis towards the Saudi capital of Riyadh, where residents and an AFP journalist heard an explosion. It also said it had destroyed a cruise missile launched towards the west of the country and a drone in the Jeddah region on the Red Sea. "The air force of the Saudi enemy today launched a series of strikes at the capital Sanaa," the Houthis' press agency reported on Thursday morning. An AFP journalist in Sanaa reported seeing smoke in the area of the airport. The Houthi news outlet Almasirah reported that the strikes targeted a factory and warehouses in Bani al-Harith. Later on Thursday (November 26, 2026), residents of the key Houthi-controlled port of Hodeida told AFP they had heard jets flying over the city and loud explosions. Almasirah said the strikes destroyed a wastewater treatment facility serving a densely populated district. The Houthis said the day before they had struck two Saudi ports on the Red Sea, after Saudi strikes on Hodeida.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The coalition, meanwhile, said it had brought down a Houthi projectile targeting Jazan that had caused light damage and no civilian casualties.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #20 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 Yemen's Houthi-held capital hit after group targets Riyadh

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 11:09:34 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The exchanges between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen have become near-daily in the country's revived civil war

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Houthi media reported a series of Saudi airstrikes against territory held by the Iran-backed group including the capital Sanaa on Thursday (November 26, 2026), hours after it struck Riyadh. The exchanges between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen have become near-daily in the country's revived civil war, which first began more than a decade ago. The coalition, which backs Yemen's internationally recognised government, said during the night that it had intercepted two ballistic missiles launched by the Houthis towards the Saudi capital of Riyadh, where residents and an AFP journalist heard an explosion. It also said it had destroyed a cruise missile launched towards the west of the country and a drone in the Jeddah region on the Red Sea. "The air force of the Saudi enemy today launched a series of strikes at the capital Sanaa," the Houthis' press agency reported on Thursday morning. An AFP journalist in Sanaa reported seeing smoke in the area of the airport. The Houthi news outlet Almasirah reported that the strikes targeted a factory and warehouses in Bani al-Harith. Later on Thursday (November 26, 2026), residents of the key Houthi-controlled port of Hodeida told AFP they had heard jets flying over the city and loud explosions. Almasirah said the strikes destroyed a wastewater treatment facility serving a densely populated district. The Houthis said the day before they had struck two Saudi ports on the Red Sea, after Saudi strikes on Hodeida.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The coalition, meanwhile, said it had brought down a Houthi projectile targeting Jazan that had caused light damage and no civilian casualties.

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Medics said an Israeli airstrike hit an apartment in Deir Al-Balah in central Gaza Strip, killing ‌Khaled Abu Nada, the Deputy Gaza Education Minister, and his wife.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Israeli airstrikes ‌and gunfire killed at least nine Palestinians overnight, medics said, including the ​Hamas-appointed deputy minister of education in the Gaza Strip, in ⁠a third consecutive night of air attacks despite a one-year-old ceasefire. Medics said an Israeli airstrike hit an apartment in Deir Al-Balah in central Gaza Strip on Thursday, killing ‌Khaled Abu Nada, the deputy Gaza education minister, and his wife. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the attack was one of ‌a series of targeted killings carried out recently against members and ‌senior ⁠officials in Hamas, adding that Israel has killed about 80 ⁠Hamas militants in the past month. "No terrorist is immune, and no one in the Hamas leadership will manage to evade us," said Mr. Netanyahu. The Israeli military said Abu Nada oversaw ​Hamas' economic portfolio and managed its ‌banking and investment network, directing funds toward militant activities and force buildup. The military said his death may weaken the group's ability to sustain its finances and support its military capabilities. Hamas confirmed the death but had ‌no immediate comment on the allegations about his role. Two other separate ​airstrikes killed six people in Tuffah neighbourhood and Beach refugee camp overnight in Gaza City, medics added. Later on Thursday (November 26, 2026), ⁠medics said Israeli gunfire killed a 62-year-old man in eastern Bureij refugee camp. The Israeli military didn't immediately comment on those seven reported deaths. Israel has continued to ‌carry out attacks that it says target Hamas but which have also killed many civilians. The broader ceasefire plan, backed by U.S. President Donald Trump, has not halted the violence or secured Hamas' disarmament. Abu Nada was the third senior Hamas official Israel has killed since Tuesday, after two senior security officials.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: At least 1,600 Palestinians and 5 Israeli soldiers have been killed ‌since the ceasefire was agreed in October 2025, according to respective Palestinian and Israeli tallies.

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 11:05:25 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Medics said an Israeli airstrike hit an apartment in Deir Al-Balah in central Gaza Strip, killing ‌Khaled Abu Nada, the Deputy Gaza Education Minister, and his wife.

2. Medics said an Israeli airstrike hit an apartment in Deir Al-Balah in central Gaza Strip on Thursday, killing ‌Khaled Abu Nada, the deputy Gaza education minister, and his wife. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the attack was one of ‌a series of targeted killings carried out recently against members and ‌senior ⁠officials in Hamas, adding that Israel has killed about 80 ⁠Hamas militants in the past month. "No terrorist is immune, and no one in the Hamas leadership will manage to evade us," said Mr. Netanyahu. The Israeli military said Abu Nada oversaw ​Hamas' economic portfolio and managed its ‌banking and investment network, directing funds toward militant activities and force buildup. The military said his death may weaken the group's ability to sustain its finances and support its military capabilities. Hamas confirmed the death but had ‌no immediate comment on the allegations about his role. articles.title: Nvidia stops shipping AI servers to four Southeast Asian nations
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Financial Times report said Nvidia had instructed manufacturing partners to stop shipping computer servers to buyers in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: U.S. tech titan Nvidia is not allowing orders of computer servers containing its artificial intelligence chips to be shipped to four Southeast Asian countries, the Financial Times reported Thursday (November 26, 2026). The article comes after Washington tightened export controls for the sensitive components in the wake of an espionage scandal that has engulfed Nvidia, forcing out longtime CEO Jensen Huang before his reinstatement on Sunday (November 22, 2026). Citing national security concerns, the United States has since 2022 restricted export to tech rival China of Nvidia's industry-leading advanced chips that are used to train and run AI tools. Washington last week moved to close a loophole in those controls, to crack down on chip smuggling, but also the large grey market of Chinese companies renting computing power from data centres in third countries, often in Southeast Asia. The Financial Times report said Nvidia had instructed manufacturing partners to stop shipping computer servers to buyers in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia. The British newspaper, citing three people with knowledge of the matter, said it was unclear whether the halt was temporary. What are AI PCs that Nvidia's Jensen Huang is betting on? Nvidia's web of AI bets: smart strategy or bubble risk? It named U.S. giants Dell and Supermicro, who package Nvidia AI chips into servers for data centres, as two affected partners.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Buyers affected include Singapore-based cloud computing company Aolani, which had planned to provide access to the Nvidia hardware to Chinese TikTok owner ByteDance through leasing agreements, the Financial Times said.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #22 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 Nvidia stops shipping AI servers to four Southeast Asian nations

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 10:56:12 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The Financial Times report said Nvidia had instructed manufacturing partners to stop shipping computer servers to buyers in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: U.S. tech titan Nvidia is not allowing orders of computer servers containing its artificial intelligence chips to be shipped to four Southeast Asian countries, the Financial Times reported Thursday (November 26, 2026). The article comes after Washington tightened export controls for the sensitive components in the wake of an espionage scandal that has engulfed Nvidia, forcing out longtime CEO Jensen Huang before his reinstatement on Sunday (November 22, 2026). Citing national security concerns, the United States has since 2022 restricted export to tech rival China of Nvidia's industry-leading advanced chips that are used to train and run AI tools. Washington last week moved to close a loophole in those controls, to crack down on chip smuggling, but also the large grey market of Chinese companies renting computing power from data centres in third countries, often in Southeast Asia. The Financial Times report said Nvidia had instructed manufacturing partners to stop shipping computer servers to buyers in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia. The British newspaper, citing three people with knowledge of the matter, said it was unclear whether the halt was temporary. What are AI PCs that Nvidia's Jensen Huang is betting on? Nvidia's web of AI bets: smart strategy or bubble risk? It named U.S. giants Dell and Supermicro, who package Nvidia AI chips into servers for data centres, as two affected partners.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Buyers affected include Singapore-based cloud computing company Aolani, which had planned to provide access to the Nvidia hardware to Chinese TikTok owner ByteDance through leasing agreements, the Financial Times said.

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Ukraine sank a Russian naval corvette in a Libyan port using maritime drones on Sunday, a day after ​it carried out a ‌drone strike on a Russian military-linked cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Kremlin on Thursday (November 26, 2026) accused Ukraine of trying to spread ​the war it is fighting against Russia to the Mediterranean ‌and Baltics seas, a move it called very dangerous. U.S. ​President Donald Trump and NATO chief Mark ⁠Rutte said in a joint statement on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) after a meeting in Florida that Russia should avoid actions that expand its full-scale ‌war in Ukraine, which it launched in 2022. Their intervention appeared to be a warning to Moscow ‌to think twice about how it retaliated against ‌Ukraine ⁠over recent attacks Kyiv has launched on Russian interests ⁠far from the conflict zone. Ukraine sank a Russian naval corvette in a Libyan port using maritime drones on Sunday, a day after ​it carried out a ‌drone strike on a Russian military-linked cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland. Responding to the joint U.S.-NATO statement, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said that nobody wanted the conflict ‌to expand, but he said Ukraine, not Russia was ​the one trying to widen the area of conflict. "As regards the escalation of the conflict in ⁠Ukraine, this appears to refer to attempts by the Kyiv regime to expand the geographical scope of this conflict. We ‌are witnessing terrorist activity by the Kyiv regime in the Mediterranean and the Baltic," Mr. Peskov told reporters on a conference call. Ukraine says it struck two oil refineries in Russia's Samara region Russia dusts off its pre-war demands as the U.S. raises discussing European security at Ukraine talks "This cannot fail to cause concern amongst coastal states, and most likely within the Alliance as a whole, the North Atlantic Treaty Organization. Of course, nobody would ‌want the conflict to spread geographically, and these are potentially very dangerous ​actions on the part of the Kyiv regime,” he added.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Libyan authorities condemned Ukraine's actions, as did ⁠Italy which told Kyiv it was wrong to attack Russian ships ⁠in Libyan waters and warned it not to spread the war to new areas. Norway, a strong ‌supporter of Kyiv, also urged it to exercise caution in any Baltic Sea operations and stressed the ​need to maintain stability in areas close to it.

Their intervention appeared to be a warning to Moscow ‌to think twice about how it retaliated against ‌Ukraine ⁠over recent attacks Kyiv has launched on Russian interests ⁠far from the conflict zone. Ukraine sank a Russian naval corvette in a Libyan port using maritime drones on Sunday, a day after ​it carried out a ‌drone strike on a Russian military-linked cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland. Responding to the joint U.S.-NATO statement, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said that nobody wanted the conflict ‌to expand, but he said Ukraine, not Russia was ​the one trying to widen the area of conflict. "As regards the escalation of the conflict in ⁠Ukraine, this appears to refer to attempts by the Kyiv regime to expand the geographical scope of this conflict. We ‌are witnessing terrorist activity by the Kyiv regime in the Mediterranean and the Baltic," Mr. Peskov told reporters on a conference call. 3. articles.title: Myanmar says it will not fully comply with ICJ genocide orders
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The ruling by ‌the ⁠ICJ, the first instance of the UN court holding a ⁠state responsible for genocide, is final but the court has very limited options to enforce it

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Myanmar's military-backed ‌President has said his administration will not comply with all ​measures ordered by the UN's top court, which last ⁠week ruled that the country's security forces had committed genocide against the Rohingya. The International Court of Justice (ICJ) found that the Myanmar military's actions against the mainly ‌Muslim Rohingya minority in 2017, including thousands of killings, the burning of hundreds of villages and widespread sexual violence, amounted ‌to genocide — and ordered a slew of measures. The ruling by ‌the ⁠ICJ, the first instance of the UN court holding a ⁠state responsible for genocide, is final but the court has very limited options to enforce it. "Myanmar would take actions appropriate for a responsible country but would not comply with requirements it considered inappropriate," he said in a meeting on ‌Wednesday, according to state media. Min Aung Hlaing did not elaborate ​on what court orders his administration considered inappropriate. The ICJ has ordered Myanmar to end ongoing breaches of the Genocide ⁠Convention and promptly investigate, prosecute and punish people reasonably suspected of involvement in the 2017 military operations. It also ordered the country to provide guarantees ‌that such violations will not be repeated. Myanmar must also facilitate the return of displaced Rohingya, restore or replace lost property, help locate missing people, provide rehabilitation to survivors, and protect Rohingya from discrimination and persecution. The court further ordered Myanmar to pay compensation for the harm caused to Rohingya that is not remedied through restitution. Myanmar must report ‌back within two years on the measures it has taken, including proposed compensation, ​the order said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Myanmar has maintained that operations undertaken by its security forces in northern Rakhine state during 2016–2018 ⁠were counter-terrorism actions against an insurgent group.

hinglishTracks.en: The ruling by ‌the ⁠ICJ, the first instance of the UN court holding a ⁠state responsible for genocide, is final but the court has very limited options to enforce it
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — ⁠आईसीजे का फैसला, संयुक्त राष्ट्र अदालत द्वारा किसी राज्य को नरसंहार के लिए जिम्मेदार ठहराने का पहला मामला, अंतिम है लेकिन अदालत के पास इसे लागू करने के लिए बहुत सीमित विकल्प हैं।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Enforcement' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: सख्ती से कानून लागू करना — किसी नियम या आदेश का ज़मीनी स्तर पर पालन करवाना। इसके Synonyms हैं: Implementation, Execution, Administration और Antonyms हैं: Neglect, Abandonment, Waiver।

hinglishTracks.en: The International Court of Justice (ICJ) found that the Myanmar military's actions against the mainly ‌Muslim Rohingya minority in 2017, including thousands of killings, the burning of hundreds of villages and widespread sexual violence, amounted ‌to genocide — and ordered a slew of measures.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — अंतर्राष्ट्रीय न्यायालय (आईसीजे) ने पाया कि 2017 में मुख्य रूप से मुस्लिम रोहिंग्या अल्पसंख्यक के खिलाफ म्यांमार सेना की कार्रवाई, जिसमें हजारों हत्याएं, सैकड़ों गांवों को जलाना और व्यापक यौन हिंसा शामिल थी, नरसंहार के बराबर थी - और कई उपायों का आदेश दिया।।

hinglishTracks.en: "Myanmar would take actions appropriate for a responsible country but would not comply with requirements it considered inappropriate," he said in a meeting on ‌Wednesday, according to state media.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — राज्य मीडिया के अनुसार, बुधवार को एक बैठक में उन्होंने कहा, "म्यांमार एक जिम्मेदार देश के लिए उचित कार्रवाई करेगा, लेकिन अनुचित समझी जाने वाली आवश्यकताओं का पालन नहीं करेगा।"।

hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — मिन आंग ह्लाइंग ने यह नहीं बताया कि उनके प्रशासन ने अदालत के किस आदेश को अनुचित माना है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Administration' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: प्रशासन — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Administration' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Significant, Substantial, Strategic और Antonyms हैं: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial।

hinglishTracks.en: The ICJ has ordered Myanmar to end ongoing breaches of the Genocide ⁠Convention and promptly investigate, prosecute and punish people reasonably suspected of involvement in the 2017 military operations.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — आईसीजे ने म्यांमार को नरसंहार कन्वेंशन के चल रहे उल्लंघनों को समाप्त करने और 2017 के सैन्य अभियानों में शामिल होने के संदिग्ध लोगों की तुरंत जांच करने, मुकदमा चलाने और दंडित करने का आदेश दिया है।।

hinglishTracks.en: It also ordered the country to provide guarantees ‌that such violations will not be repeated.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — इसने देश को यह गारंटी देने का भी आदेश दिया कि इस तरह के उल्लंघन दोबारा नहीं होंगे।।

hinglishTracks.en: Myanmar must also facilitate the return of displaced Rohingya, restore or replace lost property, help locate missing people, provide rehabilitation to survivors, and protect Rohingya from discrimination and persecution.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — म्यांमार को विस्थापित रोहिंग्या की वापसी की सुविधा देनी होगी, खोई हुई संपत्ति को बहाल करना या बदलना होगा, लापता लोगों का पता लगाने में मदद करनी होगी, बचे लोगों को पुनर्वास प्रदान करना होगा और रोहिंग्या को भेदभाव और उत्पीड़न से बचाना होगा।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Rehabilitation' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: पुनर्वास — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Rehabilitation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Significant, Substantial, Strategic और Antonyms हैं: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial।

hinglishTracks.en: The court further ordered Myanmar to pay compensation for the harm caused to Rohingya that is not remedied through restitution.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — अदालत ने म्यांमार को रोहिंग्या को हुए नुकसान के लिए मुआवजा देने का भी आदेश दिया, जिसकी भरपाई क्षतिपूर्ति से नहीं की जा सकती।।

hinglishTracks.en: Myanmar must report ‌back within two years on the measures it has taken, including proposed compensation, ​the order said.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — आदेश में कहा गया है कि म्यांमार को प्रस्तावित मुआवजे सहित अपने द्वारा उठाए गए कदमों पर दो साल के भीतर रिपोर्ट देनी होगी।।

hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — म्यांमार ने कहा है कि 2016-2018 के दौरान उत्तरी राखीन राज्य में उसके सुरक्षा बलों द्वारा किए गए ऑपरेशन एक विद्रोही समूह के खिलाफ आतंकवाद विरोधी कार्रवाई थी।।

Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Myanmar's military-backed ‌President has said his administration will not comply with all ​measures ordered by the UN's top court, which last ⁠week ruled that the country's security forces had committed genocide against the Rohingya. The International Court of Justice (ICJ) found that the Myanmar military's actions against the mainly ‌Muslim Rohingya minority in 2017, including thousands of killings, the burning of hundreds of villages and widespread sexual violence, amounted ‌to genocide — and ordered a slew of measures. The ruling by ‌the ⁠ICJ, the first instance of the UN court holding a ⁠state responsible for genocide, is final but the court has very limited options to enforce it. "Myanmar would take actions appropriate for a responsible country but would not comply with requirements it considered inappropriate," he said in a meeting on ‌Wednesday, according to state media. Min Aung Hlaing did not elaborate ​on what court orders his administration considered inappropriate. The ICJ has ordered Myanmar to end ongoing breaches of the Genocide ⁠Convention and promptly investigate, prosecute and punish people reasonably suspected of involvement in the 2017 military operations. It also ordered the country to provide guarantees ‌that such violations will not be repeated. Myanmar must also facilitate the return of displaced Rohingya, restore or replace lost property, help locate missing people, provide rehabilitation to survivors, and protect Rohingya from discrimination and persecution. The court further ordered Myanmar to pay compensation for the harm caused to Rohingya that is not remedied through restitution. Myanmar must report ‌back within two years on the measures it has taken, including proposed compensation, ​the order said.

articles.title: Delhi tops list of most polluted NCR cities for PM2.5, PM10 despite no severe AQI days
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The city's air quality remained in the poor or very poor categories for 30 days

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Delhi topped the list of the 10 most polluted cities in the National Capital Region for both PM2.5 and PM10 during the October 1-November 25 period this year, moving up from third and fourth positions in the corresponding period last year. According to an analysis of India Air Quality Portal by EnviroCatalysts, Delhi recorded an average PM2.5 concentration of 113 micrograms per cubic metre during the period, followed by Gurugram at 109, Noida at 105, Ghaziabad at 103, Meerut at 96, Baghpat and Greater Noida at 95, Panipat at 90, Bulandshahr at 82, and Faridabad at 69. For PM10, Delhi again topped the list with an average concentration of 221 micrograms per cubic metre. Gurugram recorded 207, followed by Bulandshahr at 201, Noida at 200, Ghaziabad at 197, Baghpat at 193, Greater Noida at 192, Meerut at 178, and Panipat and Faridabad at 173 each. In the corresponding period last year, Delhi recorded an average PM2.5 concentration of 158 micrograms per cubic metre, ranking third behind Ghaziabad and Noida. Its average PM10 concentration stood at 287 micrograms per cubic metre, placing it fourth behind Ghaziabad, Noida and Greater Noida. Ghaziabad topped both lists in 2025. A comparison of the same period over the last six years, from 2021 to 2026, shows that Delhi topped the PM2.5 list three times, in 2022, 2024 and 2026, while it recorded the highest average PM10 concentration twice, in 2024 and 2026. Despite topping both pollution charts, Delhi did not record a single day in the severe air quality category during the 56 days. It recorded three days in the satisfactory category, 23 in moderate, 18 in poor and 12 in very poor. "Air across the NCR has been clearly better this season, helped by good October rain and less pollution reaching Delhi from spread-out and fewer farm fires. The next step is to cut year-round sources such as vehicles, dust and waste burning across the whole region, so this improvement becomes the new normal," Sunil Dahiya, founder and lead analyst at EnviroCatalyst, told PTI. The city's air quality remained in the poor or very poor categories for 30 days.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In 2025, Delhi recorded four satisfactory days, nine moderate days, 13 poor days, 27 very poor days and three severe days. The previous year, air quality remained in the moderate category for 13 days, poor for 10 days, very poor for 25 days and severe for eight days.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #25 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 Delhi tops list of most polluted NCR cities for PM2.5, PM10 despite no severe AQI days

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 10:07:48 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The city's air quality remained in the poor or very poor categories for 30 days

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Delhi topped the list of the 10 most polluted cities in the National Capital Region for both PM2.5 and PM10 during the October 1-November 25 period this year, moving up from third and fourth positions in the corresponding period last year. According to an analysis of India Air Quality Portal by EnviroCatalysts, Delhi recorded an average PM2.5 concentration of 113 micrograms per cubic metre during the period, followed by Gurugram at 109, Noida at 105, Ghaziabad at 103, Meerut at 96, Baghpat and Greater Noida at 95, Panipat at 90, Bulandshahr at 82, and Faridabad at 69. For PM10, Delhi again topped the list with an average concentration of 221 micrograms per cubic metre. Gurugram recorded 207, followed by Bulandshahr at 201, Noida at 200, Ghaziabad at 197, Baghpat at 193, Greater Noida at 192, Meerut at 178, and Panipat and Faridabad at 173 each. In the corresponding period last year, Delhi recorded an average PM2.5 concentration of 158 micrograms per cubic metre, ranking third behind Ghaziabad and Noida. Its average PM10 concentration stood at 287 micrograms per cubic metre, placing it fourth behind Ghaziabad, Noida and Greater Noida. Ghaziabad topped both lists in 2025. A comparison of the same period over the last six years, from 2021 to 2026, shows that Delhi topped the PM2.5 list three times, in 2022, 2024 and 2026, while it recorded the highest average PM10 concentration twice, in 2024 and 2026. Despite topping both pollution charts, Delhi did not record a single day in the severe air quality category during the 56 days. It recorded three days in the satisfactory category, 23 in moderate, 18 in poor and 12 in very poor. "Air across the NCR has been clearly better this season, helped by good October rain and less pollution reaching Delhi from spread-out and fewer farm fires. The next step is to cut year-round sources such as vehicles, dust and waste burning across the whole region, so this improvement becomes the new normal," Sunil Dahiya, founder and lead analyst at EnviroCatalyst, told PTI. The city's air quality remained in the poor or very poor categories for 30 days.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In 2025, Delhi recorded four satisfactory days, nine moderate days, 13 poor days, 27 very poor days and three severe days. The previous year, air quality remained in the moderate category for 13 days, poor for 10 days, very poor for 25 days and severe for eight days.

✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial

सुधार — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Improvement' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Pollution (Noun)
प्रदूषण — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Pollution' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

articles.title: Mindfulness linked to healthier social media use, better mental health: study
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The findings showed that higher levels of mindfulness were associated with lower levels of depression, anxiety, stress, loneliness and fear of missing out (FoMO)

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: People with higher levels of mindfulness are more likely to have healthier social media habits and better mental health outcomes, according to a review of 43 studies involving more than 28,000 participants. Mindfulness involves observing one’s thoughts and feelings without judgement. Researchers led by University College London analysed the studies and found that people who reported being more mindful in their daily lives were more likely to report healthier patterns of social media use. The findings, published in the journal PLOS One , also showed that higher levels of mindfulness were associated with lower levels of depression, anxiety, stress, loneliness and fear of missing out (FoMO). Previous studies have shown that cultivating mindfulness through practices such as meditation or mindfulness-based therapy can help reduce symptoms of stress, anxiety and depression. The review contributes to the debate over whether social media use poses a risk to mental health or aggravates existing mental health problems, the researchers said. Lead author Dr Marc S Tibber from University College London’s Division of Psychology and Language Sciences said the findings supported a shift away from simplistic questions about whether social media was inherently good or bad. “Our findings support a move away from reductive questions about whether social media is inherently good or bad, towards an exploration of how complex interactions between individuals, technologies, and the broader social contexts in which they are embedded shape both the potential benefits and harms of social media for mental health,” Tibber said. The review suggested that mindfulness may play a protective role, he said, adding that it could be a potential target for interventions aimed at promoting healthier digital engagement, although further research was needed.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The studies included participants aged 10 to 92, with university students accounting for the largest group at 46.5 %.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #26 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 Mindfulness linked to healthier social media use, better mental health: study

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 10:05:38 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The findings showed that higher levels of mindfulness were associated with lower levels of depression, anxiety, stress, loneliness and fear of missing out (FoMO)

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: People with higher levels of mindfulness are more likely to have healthier social media habits and better mental health outcomes, according to a review of 43 studies involving more than 28,000 participants. Mindfulness involves observing one’s thoughts and feelings without judgement. Researchers led by University College London analysed the studies and found that people who reported being more mindful in their daily lives were more likely to report healthier patterns of social media use. The findings, published in the journal PLOS One , also showed that higher levels of mindfulness were associated with lower levels of depression, anxiety, stress, loneliness and fear of missing out (FoMO). Previous studies have shown that cultivating mindfulness through practices such as meditation or mindfulness-based therapy can help reduce symptoms of stress, anxiety and depression. The review contributes to the debate over whether social media use poses a risk to mental health or aggravates existing mental health problems, the researchers said. Lead author Dr Marc S Tibber from University College London’s Division of Psychology and Language Sciences said the findings supported a shift away from simplistic questions about whether social media was inherently good or bad. “Our findings support a move away from reductive questions about whether social media is inherently good or bad, towards an exploration of how complex interactions between individuals, technologies, and the broader social contexts in which they are embedded shape both the potential benefits and harms of social media for mental health,” Tibber said. The review suggested that mindfulness may play a protective role, he said, adding that it could be a potential target for interventions aimed at promoting healthier digital engagement, although further research was needed.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The studies included participants aged 10 to 92, with university students accounting for the largest group at 46.5 %.

articles.title: Infectious diseases from free-ranging domestic animals threaten Nilgiris wildlife
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Five of the 12 reported instances of wildlife deaths since 2005 likely due to infections contracted from feral animals were recorded in the Nilgiris district, shows report by Forest Department

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Frequent interactions between wildlife and free-ranging domestic animals raise concerns about disease transmission to wildlife in the Nilgiris. According to a report submitted by the Forest Department to the Madras High Court, five of the 12 reported instances of infections that caused wildlife deaths, likely due to interactions with feral animals, since 2005 were recorded in the Nilgiris district. Necropsy on wildlife carcasses had found canine distemper and rabies as the cause of deaths, which had been reported in the Nilgiris, Gudalur and Mudumalai Tiger Reserve (MTR) forest divisions. S. Muralidharan, who is appearing as the party-in-person before the High Court, has sought judicial intervention to address the threat to wildlife. He told The Hindu that there have been instances of diseases such as canine distemper and rabies spreading to wildlife from free-ranging domestic animals, particularly dogs. He pointed out that such diseases had threatened the survival of vulnerable wildlife populations, citing outbreaks of canine distemper among Asiatic lions in Gujarat as an example of the potential consequences. “This is a very serious concern, especially in areas where there is a very high interface between wildlife and human communities, which feed and maintain free-ranging dog populations, like in the Nilgiris” he said. Mr. Muralidharan called on the government to take measures to manage free-ranging dogs and cats in areas bordering tiger reserves and reserve forests across the State, including their removal from these areas to protect wildlife. “These animals also hunt small game such as birds and even deer and can be extremely aggressive,” he said. According to the report filed by the Forest Department, the deaths of the 12 animals reported due to transmission of disease from domestic animals include those of leopards (canine distemper), Nilgiri langur (rabies), Indian gaur (rabies), sloth bear (rabies and ehrlichiosis) and golden jackals (canine distemper and parvovirus infection). Conservationists said that the number of animals dying from diseases transmitted to wildlife from feral animals could be much higher as not all wildlife deaths are reported or are noticed if they occur inside reserve forests.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The deaths had been reported in Kodaikanal, Kalakkad Mundanthurai Tiger Reserve (KMTR), Sivaganga, Theni, Kanniyakumari and Tirunelveli, but the Nilgiris had the highest number of the reported deaths.

Mr. Muralidharan called on the government to take measures to manage free-ranging dogs and cats in areas bordering tiger reserves and reserve forests across the State, including their removal from these areas to protect wildlife. “These animals also hunt small game such as birds and even deer and can be extremely aggressive,” he said. According to the report filed by the Forest Department, the deaths of the 12 animals reported due to transmission of disease from domestic animals include those of leopards (canine distemper), Nilgiri langur (rabies), Indian gaur (rabies), sloth bear (rabies and ehrlichiosis) and golden jackals (canine distemper and parvovirus infection). Conservationists said that the number of animals dying from diseases transmitted to wildlife from feral animals could be much higher as not all wildlife deaths are reported or are noticed if they occur inside reserve forests.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The deaths had been reported in Kodaikanal, Kalakkad Mundanthurai Tiger Reserve (KMTR), Sivaganga, Theni, Kanniyakumari and Tirunelveli, but the Nilgiris had the highest number of the reported deaths.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #27 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 Infectious diseases from free-ranging domestic animals threaten Nilgiris wildlife

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 09:24:03 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Five of the 12 reported instances of wildlife deaths since 2005 likely due to infections contracted from feral animals were recorded in the Nilgiris district, shows report by Forest Department

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Frequent interactions between wildlife and free-ranging domestic animals raise concerns about disease transmission to wildlife in the Nilgiris. According to a report submitted by the Forest Department to the Madras High Court, five of the 12 reported instances of infections that caused wildlife deaths, likely due to interactions with feral animals, since 2005 were recorded in the Nilgiris district. Necropsy on wildlife carcasses had found canine distemper and rabies as the cause of deaths, which had been reported in the Nilgiris, Gudalur and Mudumalai Tiger Reserve (MTR) forest divisions. S. Muralidharan, who is appearing as the party-in-person before the High Court, has sought judicial intervention to address the threat to wildlife. articles.title: Training vs inference: What’s the distinction at the heart of the Sarvam AI-China models controversy? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Can India build an indigenous AI ecosystem while hosting models developed in China? What is Sarvam’s Token Factory? What does it mean for India’s AI ambitions?

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The story so far: Sarvam AI has so far been known for developing its own Artificial Intelligence (AI) models with support from the government’s IndiaAI Mission . On November 16, the Bengaluru-based startup added another part to its business with the launch of Token Factory, a commercial service that gives businesses access to its own models and those developed by other companies, including Chinese firms. The launch prompted a debate over whether offering Chinese-developed models through a commercial platform aligns with India’s ambition to build indigenous AI capabilities, particularly when a company has received government support. Hemant Mohapatra, partner at Lightspeed India and an investor in Sarvam, defended the commercial rationale. In a November 18 post on X, he said global AI companies were generating substantial revenue by hosting models, including Chinese ones, on infrastructure in India and serving customers worldwide. He attributed the opportunity to a global shortage of GPUs, which has made computing capacity in India attractive to companies seeking to run their models. On November 22, Sarvam co-founder Pratyush Kumar issued a clarification on X, addressing questions about the company’s government support, its decision to host foreign-developed models and its commitment to developing its own models. He said Sarvam had used subsidised computing access under the IndiaAI Mission to train its 105B model, while maintaining that its inference business did not conflict with its objective of developing its own models. The government has also defended Sarvam’s commercial strategy. IT Secretary S Krishnan told reporters that the Centre did not see any misuse of IndiaAI Mission support in the company’s decision to offer foreign-developed models through Token Factory. “Based on what Sarvam has told us, based on the experience that people have, we do not see any misuse of the support, which the IndiaAI Mission has provided to Sarvam in the service that they are now offering,” he said. Krishnan said there was no contradiction between developing indigenous models and offering foreign-developed ones commercially, adding that AI companies also needed a revenue model. Token Factory is an inference platform that allows developers and businesses to access several AI models through a single Application Programming Interface (API). An API allows one software application to communicate with another. Instead of setting up and managing the infrastructure needed to run a model, a business can connect its software to Sarvam’s API and send requests to the model it wants to use. The platform offers Sarvam’s 105-billion-parameter model, alongside open-weight models such as GLM 5.3 and GLM 5.3 Flash from China’s Z.ai, DeepSeek V4 models from DeepSeek, Kimi models from Moonshot AI, and Google’s Gemma 4 31B. Open-weight models are those whose trained parameters, or weights, are made available for others to download and run. Businesses can use them without having to develop the models from scratch.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Sarvam says Token Factory runs the models on GPU clusters located in India. Customers pay according to the number of tokens processed.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #28 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 Training vs inference: What’s the distinction at the heart of the Sarvam AI-China models controversy? | Explained

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 08:58:24 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Can India build an indigenous AI ecosystem while hosting models developed in China? What is Sarvam’s Token Factory? What does it mean for India’s AI ambitions?

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The story so far: Sarvam AI has so far been known for developing its own Artificial Intelligence (AI) models with support from the government’s IndiaAI Mission . On November 16, the Bengaluru-based startup added another part to its business with the launch of Token Factory, a commercial service that gives businesses access to its own models and those developed by other companies, including Chinese firms. The launch prompted a debate over whether offering Chinese-developed models through a commercial platform aligns with India’s ambition to build indigenous AI capabilities, particularly when a company has received government support. Hemant Mohapatra, partner at Lightspeed India and an investor in Sarvam, defended the commercial rationale. In a November 18 post on X, he said global AI companies were generating substantial revenue by hosting models, including Chinese ones, on infrastructure in India and serving customers worldwide. He attributed the opportunity to a global shortage of GPUs, which has made computing capacity in India attractive to companies seeking to run their models. On November 22, Sarvam co-founder Pratyush Kumar issued a clarification on X, addressing questions about the company’s government support, its decision to host foreign-developed models and its commitment to developing its own models. He said Sarvam had used subsidised computing access under the IndiaAI Mission to train its 105B model, while maintaining that its inference business did not conflict with its objective of developing its own models. The government has also defended Sarvam’s commercial strategy. IT Secretary S Krishnan told reporters that the Centre did not see any misuse of IndiaAI Mission support in the company’s decision to offer foreign-developed models through Token Factory. “Based on what Sarvam has told us, based on the experience that people have, we do not see any misuse of the support, which the IndiaAI Mission has provided to Sarvam in the service that they are now offering,” he said. Krishnan said there was no contradiction between developing indigenous models and offering foreign-developed ones commercially, adding that AI companies also needed a revenue model. Token Factory is an inference platform that allows developers and businesses to access several AI models through a single Application Programming Interface (API). An API allows one software application to communicate with another. Instead of setting up and managing the infrastructure needed to run a model, a business can connect its software to Sarvam’s API and send requests to the model it wants to use. The platform offers Sarvam’s 105-billion-parameter model, alongside open-weight models such as GLM 5.3 and GLM 5.3 Flash from China’s Z.ai, DeepSeek V4 models from DeepSeek, Kimi models from Moonshot AI, and Google’s Gemma 4 31B. Open-weight models are those whose trained parameters, or weights, are made available for others to download and run. Businesses can use them without having to develop the models from scratch.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Sarvam says Token Factory runs the models on GPU clusters located in India. Customers pay according to the number of tokens processed.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Indigenous (Adjective)
स्वदेशी — अपने ही देश (भारत) के वैज्ञानिकों और इंजीनियरों द्वारा देश में विकसित किया गया।
✓ Syn: Domestic, Home-grown, Native  |  ✖ Ant: Imported, Foreign, Exotic
Clarification (Noun)
स्पष्टीकरण — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Clarification' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Contradiction (Noun)
विरोधाभास — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Contradiction' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Intelligence (Adjective / Verb)
बुद्धिमत्ता — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Intelligence' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🚀 Science, Tech & Environment passage on "Training vs inference: What’s the distinction at the heart of the Sarvam AI-China models controversy? | Explained", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Can India build an indigenous AI ecosystem while hosting models developed in China?.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Training vs inference: What’s the distinction at' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Training vs inference: What’s the distinction' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Training vs inference: What’s the distinction' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Can India build an indigenous AI ecosystem while hosting models developed in China?." (Hinglish Arth: क्या भारत चीन में विकसित मॉडलों की मेजबानी करते हुए एक स्वदेशी एआई पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र का निर्माण कर सकता है?)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Training vs inference: What’s the distinction at the heart of the Sarvam AI-China models controversy? | Explained"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Customers pay according to the number of tokens processed.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Customers pay according to the number of tokens processed." (Hinglish Arth: ग्राहक संसाधित टोकन की संख्या के अनुसार भुगतान करते हैं।)

articles.title: Two-thirds of adolescents in India are deficient in vitamin B12: ICMR survey
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Findings raise concerns about the long-term consequences of nutritional deficiencies across generations, particularly among children, adolescents, and pregnant women

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Nearly two-thirds of Indian adolescents are deficient in vitamin B12, a micronutrient essential for brain development, healthy nerve function, and the formation of red blood cells, according to a new national survey by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR). The findings raise concerns about the long-term consequences of nutritional deficiencies across generations, particularly among children, adolescents, and pregnant women. The Survey for Assessment of Markers of Population Health, Activity, Diet and Anthropometry (SAMPADA), conducted by ICMR’s National Institute of Nutrition during 2023–25, found vitamin B12 deficiency in 66.1% of adolescent boys and 65.4% of adolescent girls. The prevalence was 63.1% among pregnant women, 60.4% among adult men aged 20–59, and 57.4% among women aged 15–49. Even among children aged five to nine, 46.5% were deficient. The survey, which analysed over 1.7 lakh blood samples from a population of more than two lakh people across 183 districts and 35 States and Union Territories, defined deficiency as serum vitamin B12 levels below 203 pg/mL. Vitamin B12 plays a critical role in DNA synthesis, red blood cell formation, and maintenance of the protective covering around nerves. Prolonged deficiency can cause peripheral neuropathy, impaired balance, memory problems, and, in severe cases, irreversible neurological damage. In infants, severe deficiency can result in developmental delays and neurological impairment. “Research conducted in Pune over the past three decades has shown that vitamin B12 deficiency is common among adolescents and women of reproductive age, with important implications for the health of future generations. Low maternal B12 status, particularly when accompanied by high folate levels, has been associated with increased fat accumulation and insulin resistance in children, potentially predisposing them to diabetes and other non-communicable diseases later in life. These effects are believed to be linked to epigenetic programming arising from nutritional imbalances before conception and during pregnancy,’’ said Chittaranjan Yajnik, director, Diabetes Unit, KEM Hospital, Pune. He added that India must move beyond an exclusive focus on iron and folic acid and consider including physiological doses of B12 in supplementation programmes for women, alongside carefully planned food fortification, improved nutrition literacy among adolescents, particularly girls, and the generation of robust, India-specific evidence to establish appropriate nutritional requirements and interventions. The findings are particularly significant for maternal and child health, with nearly two-thirds of pregnant women showing a deficiency. Low maternal B12 levels have been associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes, including neural tube defects and low birth weight, as well as poorer offspring developmental outcomes. Vitamin B12 is found naturally in foods such as meat, fish, eggs, and dairy products. Inadequate dietary intake, particularly among people consuming predominantly plant-based diets, and impaired absorption can contribute to deficiency.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The findings also raise questions about whether India’s nutrition programmes are adequately addressing deficiencies beyond iron and folic acid. The Anemia Mukt Bharat strategy focuses substantially on iron and folic acid supplementation, testing and treatment of anaemia, deworming, and food fortification. Although fortified rice includes vitamin B12, routine B12 screening and supplementation are not central components of the programme.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #29 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 Two-thirds of adolescents in India are deficient in vitamin B12: ICMR survey

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 08:05:44 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Findings raise concerns about the long-term consequences of nutritional deficiencies across generations, particularly among children, adolescents, and pregnant women

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Nearly two-thirds of Indian adolescents are deficient in vitamin B12, a micronutrient essential for brain development, healthy nerve function, and the formation of red blood cells, according to a new national survey by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR). The findings raise concerns about the long-term consequences of nutritional deficiencies across generations, particularly among children, adolescents, and pregnant women. The Survey for Assessment of Markers of Population Health, Activity, Diet and Anthropometry (SAMPADA), conducted by ICMR’s National Institute of Nutrition during 2023–25, found vitamin B12 deficiency in 66.1% of adolescent boys and 65.4% of adolescent girls. The prevalence was 63.1% among pregnant women, 60.4% among adult men aged 20–59, and 57.4% among women aged 15–49. Even among children aged five to nine, 46.5% were deficient. The survey, which analysed over 1.7 lakh blood samples from a population of more than two lakh people across 183 districts and 35 States and Union Territories, defined deficiency as serum vitamin B12 levels below 203 pg/mL. Vitamin B12 plays a critical role in DNA synthesis, red blood cell formation, and maintenance of the protective covering around nerves. Prolonged deficiency can cause peripheral neuropathy, impaired balance, memory problems, and, in severe cases, irreversible neurological damage. In infants, severe deficiency can result in developmental delays and neurological impairment. “Research conducted in Pune over the past three decades has shown that vitamin B12 deficiency is common among adolescents and women of reproductive age, with important implications for the health of future generations. Low maternal B12 status, particularly when accompanied by high folate levels, has been associated with increased fat accumulation and insulin resistance in children, potentially predisposing them to diabetes and other non-communicable diseases later in life. These effects are believed to be linked to epigenetic programming arising from nutritional imbalances before conception and during pregnancy,’’ said Chittaranjan Yajnik, director, Diabetes Unit, KEM Hospital, Pune. He added that India must move beyond an exclusive focus on iron and folic acid and consider including physiological doses of B12 in supplementation programmes for women, alongside carefully planned food fortification, improved nutrition literacy among adolescents, particularly girls, and the generation of robust, India-specific evidence to establish appropriate nutritional requirements and interventions. The findings are particularly significant for maternal and child health, with nearly two-thirds of pregnant women showing a deficiency. Low maternal B12 levels have been associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes, including neural tube defects and low birth weight, as well as poorer offspring developmental outcomes. Vitamin B12 is found naturally in foods such as meat, fish, eggs, and dairy products. Inadequate dietary intake, particularly among people consuming predominantly plant-based diets, and impaired absorption can contribute to deficiency.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The findings also raise questions about whether India’s nutrition programmes are adequately addressing deficiencies beyond iron and folic acid. The Anemia Mukt Bharat strategy focuses substantially on iron and folic acid supplementation, testing and treatment of anaemia, deworming, and food fortification. Although fortified rice includes vitamin B12, routine B12 screening and supplementation are not central components of the programme.

संस्थागत — देश की संवैधानिक या सरकारी संस्थाओं के नियमों और ढांचे से जुड़ा हुआ।
✓ Syn: Systemic, Organizational, Constitutional  |  ✖ Ant: Individual, Informal, Unorganized
Supplementation (Noun)
अनुपूरण — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Supplementation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Developmental (Adjective)
विकास संबंधी — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Developmental' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Physiological (Adjective)
शारीरिक — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Physiological' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

A. Findings raise concerns about the long-term consequences of nutritional deficiencies across generations, particularly among children, adolescents,...

D. The author contends that 'Two-thirds of adolescents in India are defici' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Findings raise concerns about the long-term consequences of nutritional deficiencies across generations, particularly among children, adolescents,..." A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Although fortified rice includes vitamin B12, routine B12 screening and supplementation are not central components of the programme.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Although fortified rice includes vitamin B12, routine B12 screening and supplementation are not central components of the programme." (Hinglish Arth: हालाँकि फोर्टिफाइड चावल में विटामिन बी12 शामिल है, नियमित बी12 स्क्रीनिंग और अनुपूरण कार्यक्रम के केंद्रीय घटक नहीं हैं।)

articles.title: Spinning wheels: on urban mobility in Karnataka
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Karnataka needs a coherent policy on urban mobility

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: While Karnataka has spent years disputing motorcycle owners’ right to carry paying passengers, Bengaluru — with the dubious distinction of having one of the world’s highest travel times per unit distance — struggles with inadequate public transport capacity and lacklustre intermediate options. The Supreme Court ruling on November 20 to dismiss Karnataka’s appeal was thus straightforward, allowing motorcycles to be registered as transport vehicles. The State has often called bike taxis unsafe, yet has not improved the prospects of safer options. Earlier this year, the Centre for Science and Environment estimated the number of buses in urban centres nationwide to be 70% short of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs benchmark and that 400 cities with populations between a lakh and 10 lakh altogether lacked organised bus services. In March, the BMTC reported a fleet of around 7,000 buses in Bengaluru, versus the 13,000 by 2025 envisaged by the Comprehensive Mobility Plan. Expanding the number of Metro stations also creates more demand for travel to and from stations, but the operating costs of the public transport corporation expected to serve that demand are not covered by the resulting increase in rail ridership. Overall, Karnataka has struggled to set up a consistent transport policy. An expert committee recommended against bike taxis in Bengaluru for first- and last-mile connectivity and in favour of better walking infrastructure and bicycle rentals in 2019, only for the State to launch the electric bike-taxi scheme in 2021, then rescind it in 2024 over safety concerns and drivers’ disputes. The market for short booked journeys is also dysfunctional. But while allowing bike taxis could temper autorickshaw fares, the State must investigate drivers’ operating costs, the difference between the paid and the received amounts, and prevent large platforms from exploiting the market. Finally, while the Union Road Transport Ministry has reported that 46.2% of all road deaths involved two-wheeler users, two-wheelers’ safety relative to autorickshaws and cabs, by the number and distance of journeys, is unclear. The State should require aggregators to report injuries and fatalities and investigate the consequences of drivers’ earnings being linked to the number of trips undertaken. The Union government’s 2025 Motor Vehicle Aggregator Guidelines already address passenger security, fares, and insurance while allowing States to authorise privately registered motorcycles through aggregators. Karnataka should exercise this additional power. A large national programme is required to address funding for public transport, which is necessary even when it is not immediately profitable.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Karnataka / scooters and motorbikes / public transport / court / population / urban planning / Bengaluru Metro / Electric vehicles / road accident / road transport / insurance

hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — एक विशेषज्ञ समिति ने बेंगलुरु में पहले और आखिरी मील कनेक्टिविटी के लिए बाइक टैक्सियों के खिलाफ और 2019 में बेहतर पैदल चलने वाले बुनियादी ढांचे और साइकिल किराये के पक्ष में सिफारिश की, केवल राज्य के लिए 2021 में इलेक्ट्रिक बाइक-टैक्सी योजना शुरू की, फिर सुरक्षा चिंताओं और ड्राइवरों के विवादों पर इसे 2024 में रद्द कर दिया।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Connectivity' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: कनेक्टिविटी — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Connectivity' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Significant, Substantial, Strategic और Antonyms हैं: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial।

hinglishTracks.en: Finally, while the Union Road Transport Ministry has reported that 46.2% of all road deaths involved two-wheeler users, two-wheelers’ safety relative to autorickshaws and cabs, by the number and distance of journeys, is unclear.

✍️ Editorial & Opinion Paragraph #6 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 Spinning wheels: on urban mobility in Karnataka

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 12:02:31 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Karnataka needs a coherent policy on urban mobility

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: While Karnataka has spent years disputing motorcycle owners’ right to carry paying passengers, Bengaluru — with the dubious distinction of having one of the world’s highest travel times per unit distance — struggles with inadequate public transport capacity and lacklustre intermediate options. The Supreme Court ruling on November 20 to dismiss Karnataka’s appeal was thus straightforward, allowing motorcycles to be registered as transport vehicles. The State has often called bike taxis unsafe, yet has not improved the prospects of safer options. Earlier this year, the Centre for Science and Environment estimated the number of buses in urban centres nationwide to be 70% short of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs benchmark and that 400 cities with populations between a lakh and 10 lakh altogether lacked organised bus services. In March, the BMTC reported a fleet of around 7,000 buses in Bengaluru, versus the 13,000 by 2025 envisaged by the Comprehensive Mobility Plan. Expanding the number of Metro stations also creates more demand for travel to and from stations, but the operating costs of the public transport corporation expected to serve that demand are not covered by the resulting increase in rail ridership. Overall, Karnataka has struggled to set up a consistent transport policy. An expert committee recommended against bike taxis in Bengaluru for first- and last-mile connectivity and in favour of better walking infrastructure and bicycle rentals in 2019, only for the State to launch the electric bike-taxi scheme in 2021, then rescind it in 2024 over safety concerns and drivers’ disputes. The market for short booked journeys is also dysfunctional. But while allowing bike taxis could temper autorickshaw fares, the State must investigate drivers’ operating costs, the difference between the paid and the received amounts, and prevent large platforms from exploiting the market. Finally, while the Union Road Transport Ministry has reported that 46.2% of all road deaths involved two-wheeler users, two-wheelers’ safety relative to autorickshaws and cabs, by the number and distance of journeys, is unclear. The State should require aggregators to report injuries and fatalities and investigate the consequences of drivers’ earnings being linked to the number of trips undertaken. The Union government’s 2025 Motor Vehicle Aggregator Guidelines already address passenger security, fares, and insurance while allowing States to authorise privately registered motorcycles through aggregators. Karnataka should exercise this additional power. A large national programme is required to address funding for public transport, which is necessary even when it is not immediately profitable.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Karnataka / scooters and motorbikes / public transport / court / population / urban planning / Bengaluru Metro / Electric vehicles / road accident / road transport / insurance

✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile

बेकार — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Dysfunctional' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Connectivity (Noun)
कनेक्टिविटी — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Connectivity' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

A. Karnataka needs a coherent policy on urban mobility.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Spinning wheels: on urban mobility in Karnataka' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Spinning wheels: on urban mobility in Karnata' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Spinning wheels: on urban mobility in Karnata' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Karnataka needs a coherent policy on urban mobility." (Hinglish Arth: कर्नाटक को शहरी गतिशीलता पर एक सुसंगत नीति की आवश्यकता है)

C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. articles.title: Court rejects PG operator’s bail in Satya Niketan building collapse case, says he put profits above students’ lives
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: ‘The accused persons, who are responsible for the loss of seven valuable lives, are not entitled to the benefit of discretion and such incidents must be dealt with by the courts of law with an iron hand,’ the court said

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Observing that he appeared to have placed financial gains above the safety of students and labourers staying at the premises, a Delhi court on Monday refused to grant bail to Shubham Tyagi, one of operator of the paying guest (PG) accommodation in South Delhi’s Satya Niketan which collapsed in September this year leaving seven dead. Additional Sessions Judge Dhirendra Rana of Patiala House Court denied bail to the accuse after rejecting Mr Tyagi’s argument that he had no responsibility for the construction of the PG which he has co-accused Sudhanshu Kumar had rented the property from its owners and operated a boy’s hostel. It added that even if the construction was not being carried out under Mr Tyagi’s instructions, he was obligated to ensure that residents vacated the building until the work was completed. He was also expected to alert occupants about the potential structural danger. “The accused persons, who are responsible for the loss of seven valuable lives, are not entitled to the benefit of discretion and such incidents must be dealt with by the courts of law with an iron hand,” court said. Holding that Mr Tyagi could have anticipated the risks arising from alleged unauthorised construction and structural alterations court mentioned the statement of injured student Nitish Chhib, court said that it was alleged that basement construction had continued for 10-12 days despite complaints from students. The residents were allegedly threatened with eviction when they objected to the work. Emphasising the gravity of the incident, the court observed that building collapses linked to illegal construction have repeatedly resulted in fatalities and must be treated seriously. It remarked that those allegedly responsible for the loss of seven lives did not deserve discretionary relief and that such incidents required a firm judicial response. Denying bail, court also stated that the trial is at an early stage and public witnesses were yet to be examined and there was a possibility of witness intimidation. The Delhi Police had filed a 638-page chargesheet in the matter earlier this month. It named building owner Hariram Gupta, his wife Urmila Gupta, their son Mahesh Gupta, labour contractor Sanoj Kumar and PG operators Mr Tyagi and Mr Kumar as accused.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: India / Delhi / death / accident (general) / disaster (general)

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #7 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 Court rejects PG operator’s bail in Satya Niketan building collapse case, says he put profits above students’ lives

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 02:47:27 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: ‘The accused persons, who are responsible for the loss of seven valuable lives, are not entitled to the benefit of discretion and such incidents must be dealt with by the courts of law with an iron hand,’ the court said

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Observing that he appeared to have placed financial gains above the safety of students and labourers staying at the premises, a Delhi court on Monday refused to grant bail to Shubham Tyagi, one of operator of the paying guest (PG) accommodation in South Delhi’s Satya Niketan which collapsed in September this year leaving seven dead. Additional Sessions Judge Dhirendra Rana of Patiala House Court denied bail to the accuse after rejecting Mr Tyagi’s argument that he had no responsibility for the construction of the PG which he has co-accused Sudhanshu Kumar had rented the property from its owners and operated a boy’s hostel. It added that even if the construction was not being carried out under Mr Tyagi’s instructions, he was obligated to ensure that residents vacated the building until the work was completed. He was also expected to alert occupants about the potential structural danger. “The accused persons, who are responsible for the loss of seven valuable lives, are not entitled to the benefit of discretion and such incidents must be dealt with by the courts of law with an iron hand,” court said. Holding that Mr Tyagi could have anticipated the risks arising from alleged unauthorised construction and structural alterations court mentioned the statement of injured student Nitish Chhib, court said that it was alleged that basement construction had continued for 10-12 days despite complaints from students. The residents were allegedly threatened with eviction when they objected to the work. Emphasising the gravity of the incident, the court observed that building collapses linked to illegal construction have repeatedly resulted in fatalities and must be treated seriously. It remarked that those allegedly responsible for the loss of seven lives did not deserve discretionary relief and that such incidents required a firm judicial response. Denying bail, court also stated that the trial is at an early stage and public witnesses were yet to be examined and there was a possibility of witness intimidation. The Delhi Police had filed a 638-page chargesheet in the matter earlier this month. It named building owner Hariram Gupta, his wife Urmila Gupta, their son Mahesh Gupta, labour contractor Sanoj Kumar and PG operators Mr Tyagi and Mr Kumar as accused.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: India / Delhi / death / accident (general) / disaster (general)

articles.keyPoints:
